title: Day job packing instruments and the mellophone
summary: He has packed instruments for 15 years and earlier for C.G. Conn; a mellophone is explained.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: What have you done during the day, all your life?

The Wicked. Musical instrument packer. I've been working at Well Islands now for 15 years. 15 years? Before that I worked for C.G. Conn. For the WPA, pardon, the Ions, I worked for C.G. Conn. I worked for C.G. Conn. I worked for 15 years. Packing instruments, shipping them all over all the other states. You mentioned the mellophone earlier.
A mellophone is a horn that plays in E flat and F. It is the horn that they use with a cut mouth to be similar to a trumpet or a cornet.
Jack Willis had one Saturday. Oh yeah.
It looks like a French horn. Looks like a little French horn. Yeah.
It's got bells instead of those keys.
They're lottery keys. Instead of the rotary keys, you have a straight up and down crystal. I think mellophone is the same thing or is it right?
I think I'm not sure. It must be the same, I'm not sure.
